owner.occupation: Category buyer for an airport retail group

world.bio: I buy food gifts and souvenirs for a group of shops at Changi and a few regional airports. Fifteen years in retail buying, the last six in the gifting category. Every season I walk the shelves and the same three biscuit brands look back at me. Travellers keep telling our floor staff they want real hawker names, the stalls they queue for at home, not another tin of pineapple tarts. I like products with a story that a stranger can tell in ten seconds at a gate.
skills_assets: Category buying for roughly 140 SKUs of packaged food gifts across four airport shops
Supplier onboarding checklist I wrote myself (shelf life, labelling, halal pathway, minimum order, retail margin)
Sell-through dashboard in Excel, updated weekly, with returns by brand and by month
Contacts at two logistics firms that handle ambient and chilled air freight out of Changi
A drawer of rejected samples at home that my mother in Johor refuses to let me throw away

projects.name: Heritage food gifting range (working title)
projects.text: Next year's shelf is meant to be the 'Taste of Singapore' wall near the main gates. I have a one-page rule sheet from my director: every product on it must carry a recognisable heritage name, must already be shelf-stable for twelve months, and must have a clear halal certification pathway even if it is not certified yet. Anything from a single hawker without a product format, or a white-label made by a lab with no name behind it, goes in the no pile. I have 6 slots on the wall and 2 filled (kaya jam, a bak kwa brand I am lukewarm about). Four are open and the range review is mid-December.

projects.name: Supplier scorecard v3
projects.text: Rebuilding the scorecard so that small suppliers are not punished for not having a QA department. Adding a 'lab report accepted in lieu of in-house QA' field. Half done, stuck on how to weigh packaging damage in transit.

notes.text: Walked Terminal 3 on my day off just to look at shelves like a customer. Counted: 11 facings of shortbread, 9 of pineapple tarts, 7 of the same three-flavour cookie tin. A Japanese tourist asked the assistant if there was anything 'from a hawker'. She had to say no. I felt it in my chest a bit. This is literally my job.

Half marathon training: 16 km long run, knee fine, shoulders not. Pace was 6:40 which is still slower than I want. Ate two kaya toasts after, so net zero. Mum called while I was stretching and asked if I'd eaten properly. I lied.

Mum's cough again. Flying to Johor Friday night instead of Saturday so I can take her to the clinic Saturday morning. Brother says it's nothing. Brother lives in Perth and says it's nothing about everything.

Bought two Peranakan tiles at the Joo Chiat flea market, a pink lotus and a green one with a chip. $18 for both. The seller said the chipped one is 'more honest'. I do not have a wall for them. I have a box under the bed with 31 of them now.

Tasting session with a family biscuit maker from Geylang. Lovely people, lovely butter cookies, but she makes them to order in a flat kitchen and the shelf life is eight weeks. Told her kindly it can't go on our wall. She said 'okay lah, thank you for trying'. I hate these meetings.

Director asked again why the heritage wall has only two products. I said the rule sheet is tight and he said the rule sheet is the rule sheet. The honest problem: the people with the names don't have the format, and the people with the format don't have the names. I keep writing this sentence in my notebook as if it will turn into a supplier.
Run 18 km. Blister on left heel. Registered for the December half, so no backing out. Also reminder to renew the lease on the storage unit with the tiles and the baby clothes I cannot give away.

Made a list of hawker stalls I would actually buy a gift from: laksa on Joo Chiat, the kueh lady at Tiong Bahru, chilli crab paste from the Sembawang one, bak chor mee sauce. None of them make anything that lasts a month in a bag. Ordered the sauce anyway as a personal treat and it leaked in my luggage.

messages.text:
Priya: Did the director say yes to extending the heritage shelf deadline?
Me: No. Same rule: twelve months shelf-stable, a halal pathway, a recognised name. He doesn't want a hawker alone and he doesn't want a lab brand.
Priya: So basically he wants a miracle.
Me: He wants Ah Hock's recipe in a pouch. Don't we all.

Mum: Your brother sent a picture of the cake he baked. Why can't you bake?
Me: Mum, I buy biscuits for a living.
Mum: That's not the same as baking.
Me: It's exactly the same except I don't have to wash the tray.

Daniel: Sunday long run, 6am at East Coast? 20km target.
Me: I'll do 18 and a bit of ego. Is the new gel any good?
Daniel: Tastes like lemon sherbet that lost an argument.
Me: Sold.

Contact: For the new year we can do consolidated ambient pallets Singapore to Changi from Johor twice a week.
Me: Good, but only for ambient. I can't list anything chilled.
Contact: Understood. Every buyer says the same until the product is chilled.

calendar.event: Supplier tasting, kaya and chilli paste candidates, back office Terminal 2
Flight to Johor Bahru to see Mum (clinic follow-up)
Long run 20 km, East Coast Park, 6am
Heritage wall mid-review with director, slides due Oct 21

relations.about: Lives alone, stubborn, cough since August. I fly over most weekends.
Does not visit, sends photos of baked goods.
Good ally, tells me what the director actually thinks.

constraints: Only products that are shelf-stable for twelve months and have a halal pathway can go on the heritage wall
Flights to Johor on weekends take my free time
sensitive: I am frightened by Mum's cough and don't say it
Sometimes I feel the director measures me against the old buyer, who left on a high
I have not told anyone I'm tired of the job itself

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Role as a category buyer in airport retail, the interest in real hawker names, the half marathon and the tile hobby.
disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: The heritage shelf rules (12-month shelf life, halal pathway, recognised name), the open slots and review dates, margin and order-size ranges.
disclosure_policy.t2_after_trust: Pressure from the director, what has already failed, the family situation with Mum.
disclosure_policy.never: Mum's medical details, her salary and bonus, internal margin tables.
